Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

per preposition

for each: a head, a day

also a head, apiece, each, a day, a year, twice a day, per head

classical

Liv. 2.33.11: sextantibus conlātīs in capita
Cic. Font. 9: quaternōs dēnāriōs in singulās vīnī amphorās (Lewis & Short)

in + acc.

preposition with the accusative, often with singulī

per, for each (person or thing)

“So much a head” is in capita or in singulōs. The amount is often a distributive numeral (singulī, bīnī, ternī, quaternī): trecēnōs … in capita, three hundred a head.

Other words

  • in + abl. — a, per (twice a day, three times a year)

    preposition with the ablative, after a numeral adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.100: bis in diē saturum fierī; Cic. Rosc. Am. 132: vix ter in annō

    semel, bis, ter in diē. “Every day” is cotīdiē, “every year” quotannīs (see every year); for “per cent”, see percent.

Examples

  • extulit eum plēbs sextantibus conlātīs in capita

    the people gave him his funeral, putting in a sixth of an as a headLiv. 2.33.11

  • pretium fore in capita equitī quīngēnōs quadrīgātōs nummōs, trecēnōs peditī, servō centēnōs

    the price would be, per head, five hundred silver pieces for a horseman, three hundred for a foot soldier, a hundred for a slaveLiv. 22.58.4

  • vīta illa beāta, quae ferēbātur, plēna Ītalicārum Syrācūsiārumque mēnsārum, nūllō modō mihi placuit, bis in diē saturum fierī

    that “happy life”, as they called it, full of Italian and Syracusan feasting, did not please me at all: to be stuffed full twice a dayCic. Tusc. 5.100

  • quī in Sallentīnīs aut in Bruttiīs habent unde vix ter in annō audīre nūntium possunt

    who have estates among the Sallentini or in Bruttium, from where they can hear news barely three times a yearCic. Rosc. Am. 132

See also percent, every year.
